Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis(s) and impression:
  - Primary concern: Suspected pulmonary embolism in the postpartum/postoperative setting.
  - Rationale: Recent cesarean delivery (4 weeks ago) with acute dyspnea and tachycardia; postpartum hypercoagulable state; clinician advised hospital evaluation to exclude PE.

- Relevant differential diagnoses (aligned with transcript and DDx):
  - Pulmonary embolism (PE) — High likelihood
  - Postpartum cardiomyopathy or acute decompensated heart failure — Medium likelihood
  - Pneumonia — Medium likelihood

- Plan summary:
  - Immediate action: Hospital evaluation recommended; patient to go to the ER (self-transport with baby) or call an ambulance if preferred; avoid further codeine at this time.
  - Monitoring: Bring essential items for baby; monitor symptoms; seek urgent assessment given postpartum status and acute SOB.
  - Treatments/tests: In ED, imaging and labs to evaluate for PE/pulmonary process; possible anticoagulation if PE confirmed (not initiated here; decisions to be made in hospital).
  - Education: Reassurance about thromboembolism risk postpartum; instructions to seek urgent care if symptoms worsen.

Management Plan

- Immediate interventions: Go to the hospital promptly; self-transport preferred by patient; take baby with them; do not take codeine until evaluated.
- Medications: No new medications started during telehealth encounter; codeine use discouraged pending hospital assessment.
- Investigations: Diagnostic workup for PE and other causes to be completed in ED (imaging, labs as determined).
- Follow-up/education: Patient advised on risk of postpartum clots and to seek urgent care; no outpatient follow-up arranged at this time.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Pulmonary embolism (PE)
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Acute dyspnea in the first weeks postpartum after cesarean section; tachycardia; clinician emphasized clot risk and ED evaluation to exclude PE.
- Postpartum cardiomyopathy or acute decompensated heart failure
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Recent postpartum period with new dyspnea and tachycardia; chest discomfort on deep inspiration; however, edema/heart failure signs not described.
- Pneumonia
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: New cough with dyspnea; infectious/inflammatory process possible; absence of fever and lack of imaging data reduce certainty.
